paragraphs: [Eruvin 91a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.91a.8) reads, “Rabbi Yochanan likewise said: Who whispered to you?”

[Tosafot](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_on_Eruvin.91a.8.2) there records a reading of M'lachashekh as one word, explaining that it refers to the unqualified Rabbi Yochanan because his birth was associated with a whisper, as in [Yoma 82b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.82b.2).[^2]

notes.text: The Yoma paragraph describes a whisper to the pregnant mother, after which Yochanan was born. “Born from a whisper” was misleadingly literal; the epithet and two-word question remain alternative readings.

Tosafot records both the two-word question and a one-word reading. It also says that Rashi omitted the words. In Yoma, Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi directs people to whisper to the pregnant woman. [Heilprin’s M’lachashekh entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1829&lang=en) refers the reader to Rabbi Yochanan’s main entry.
